2. The relevant fact in short for disposal of the Rule is that Jatindra Chandra Urang, the father of the opposite party Nos.1(ka)-1(gha) as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous (pre-emption) Case No. 118 of 1985 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act against 9(nine) opposite-parties including the petition-er (vendee) in the Court of Sub-Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur on the averments that the suit land originally belonged to Hemba Urang Hemba Dhangar and Debra Urang ©. Debra Dhangar in 8 annas share each; that Debra Urang had purchased lands in SA Khatian No. 255 and CS Khatian No. 71 from Gopal Dhangar, khatian No. 341 (CS Khatian No. 125)/SA khatian No. 242 (CS Khatian No. 65) from one Kalicharan Dhangar; that while jointly owning and possessing the properties described in schedule the said Hembra Urang died leaving Rabindra Chandra Urang, the opposite party No.2 as his legal heir and Debra Urang died leaving Jatindra Chandra Urang as his legal heir. After the death of said Hembra Urang and Debra Urang Rabindra Chandra Urang and Jatindra Chandra Urang have been owning and possessing the properties jointly without partition by metes and bounds and in this way Jatindra Chandra Urang along with Rabindra Chandra Urang became owner of the case Khatians and holdings by way of inheritance and purchase; that opposite party No. 2, Rabindra Chandra Urang secretly transferred the case land to opposite party No. 1, Md Shamsuddin by executing sale deed No. 8360 dated 30-11-76 corresponding to 14th Agrahayan, 1383 BS without serving any notice of transfer upon the pre-emptor applicant under section 89 of the Act, who being a stranger to the case land; that the pre-emptor-applicant came to know about the transfer of the case land on 1-2-77 for the first time and then he rushed to the Sub-Registrar Office at Shreepur and obtained the certified copy of the sale deed No.8360 dated on 24-2-77 and filed the case for pre-emption. 

 3. The opposite party No. 1, Md Shamsuddin contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the application for pre-emption contending, inter alia, that the case is not maintainable in its present form as the pre-emptee purchaser himself is a co-sharer to the case land by way of inheritance; that application for pre-emption is barred by law of limitation and also barred by the principles of estoppels and acquiescence, the case is also bad for defect of parties as Debra Urang died leaving behind of his 3(three) sons namely Talak Urang, Jatindra Chandra Urang and Buddu Urang alias Brajendra Urang but Jatindra Chandra Urang as pre-emptor without impleaded them as parties in the pre-emption case filed the case. It has been also contended that the pre-emptor-applicant's co-sharer ship is not in existence as he had transferred his entire share by executing a number of registered deeds and as such the pre-emption application is liable to be disallowed. 

 13. I have perused the revisional application along with other materials on record including the deposition of the witnesses and considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides. Now, let me see first whether both the. Courts below committed wrong in allowing pre-emption to a transfer to a ca-sharer whose interest in the tenancy has accused by inheritance. 

 16. On a perusal of the evidence on record, it is found that the pre-emptor Jatindra Chandra Urang himself was examined as PW 1, who in his cross-examination stated that: 

 রজব আলীর পুত্র ১নং তরফছানী সামসুদ্দিন তার পিতার সম্পত্তির মালিক হইতে পারে। এস,এ, জরিপে আমার পিতার নামের সাথে ১নং তরফছানী সামুদ্দিন গংদের নাম ২৪২নং খতিয়ানে সহ শরীক কিনা বলতে পারি না। আমার অদ্যকার দাখিলকৃত সাবেক ৬৫হালে ২৪২নং খতিয়ানে আমার পিতার নাম ও ১নং তরফছানী সামসুদ্দিন এর নাম উক্ত পরচায় একত্রে লিপিবদ্ধ হইয়াছে। ১নং তরফছানী নাঃ খতিয়ানে আগন্তক নয়, সে একজন সহশরীক। আমার মালিক হওয়ার পূর্ব হইতে এস,এ উল্লেখিত রেকর্ড মূলে ১নং তরফছানী সামসুদ্দিন নালিশী জোতে সহ অংশীদার উত্তরে মজহর সম্পূর্ণ নীরব থাকে। PW 2, Md Hanif Miah also in his croos-examination stated that: নাঃ জমি থেকে quarter মাইলের কম দূরত্বে আমার বাড়ী। SA ২৪২ নং খতিয়ানে ১নং প্রতিপক্ষ সামসুদ্দিনের নাম লিপিবদ্ধ আছে। 

 18. It is found that the pre-emptee-petitioner to prove his case examined 2(two) witnesses and exhibited a series of documents including the SA Khatian No. 242. The pre-emptee-purchaser Shamsuddin himself was examined as OPW-1, who in his deposition stated that he purchased the case land by registered deed No. 8360 dated 31-11-1976 within the full knowledge of the pre-emptor. This witness also stated that his father Rajab Ali purchased 1.40 acres of land of the case khatian from one Ram Urang and others and proved the original deed No. 4380 as 'Exhibit-Kha' dated 17-4-1942. This witness also stated that: 

 19. OPW 2, Abdul Baten stated in his deposition that the opposite party No.1, purchased the case lands from Rabindra Chandra Urang and has been owing and possessing the same by erecting house. 

 20. On assessment of the evidence both oral and documentary, it appears that the pre-emptee-purchaser is a co-sharer to the case land by inheritance prior to the pre-emptor opposite party. It is not disputed that Rajab Ali had become co-sharer in the tenancy by purchase from one of the original co-sharer and that on his death his share devolved upon his son, who is the pre-emptee petitioner. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge took the view that though the pre-emptee inherited one of the case plot among the case plots from his father, but his father did not become co-sharer by inheritance and as such, the pre-emptee can not be claimed to have got interest in the tenancy by inheritance, but he got the interest by purchase. This interpretation is palpably wrong and against the spirit of clause (a) of sub-section (10) as quoted above. 

 21. Provisions for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act are not applicable to a transfer to a co-sharer whose interest in the tenancy has accrued by inheritance or otherwise than by Purchase. This provision is clearly stated in clause (a) of sub-section (10) of section 96. This sub-section is quoted below: 

 (a) a transfer to a co-sharer in the tenancy whose interest has accrued otherwise: than by purchase;" 

 22. "Co-sharer" as referred to in this clause is a person to whom the disputed transfer has been made. Certainly, in this case, disputed transfer under the sale deed No. 8360 dated 30-11-76 corresponding to 14th Agrahayan, 1383 BS was made to this pre-emptee petitioner and not to his father. His interest in the tenancy has accrued by inheritance simply because he inherited his father's share. How and in which manner their father's interest had accrued to the tenancy is immaterial. The transfer made to the present petitioner is protected and immune from pre-emption under sub-section (10)(a). This important question of law did not receive due consideration from the trial Court as well as lower appellate Court. Therefore, I am constrained to hold that the two Courts below seriously erred in law in allowing the pre-emption application without properly applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 23. Another striking feature of this case is that PW 1 Jatindra Chandra Urang (pre-emptor) admitted in his cross-examination that his father Debra Urang died leaving behind 3 sons namely Talak Urang, Baddu Urang and Jatindra Chandra Urang although suppressing this fact Jatindra Chandra Urang as pre-emptor stated in his application for pre-emption that Debra Urang died leaving Jatindra Chandra Urang, the pre-emptor as his legal heir. All the legal heirs of Debra Urang were not impleaded either in the category of the petitioners or the opposite parties in the case I therefore, find substance in the submission of Mr Abdul Majid that the pre-emptor-opposite party No.1 at the very initial stage approached before the Court with unclean hands. 

 26. For the reasons stated above the judgment of the trial Court as well as lower appellate Court does not deserve to be sustained.
